The exemption in D1 is corroborated by speed-band evidence on the replaced optimal route: TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY recorded band 1 (0–9 km/h) from 08:46 to 09:04, i.e. severe congestion covering the optimal route at the moment the driver diverted, with no contrary evidence from alternative roads (Punggol Road and Tampines Avenue 12 both band 4).

The driver's written statement that lanes were blocked by the accident and the detour was unavoidable is consistent with, and not contradicted by, the system records of the accident and the severe congestion band.

No unexempted off-route segment remains: the 1.76 km added by the only gps-detour segment is the detour around the blocked expressway, so the refund formula in RD-2 yields $0.00 and the result for this segment is no_action, with no resulting RD-1 violation to record.

The billed fare is the metered fare for the trip actually driven on RydeTAXI and the only distance-driven element is the $2.55 corresponding to the 1.8 km of excess distance; with the segment exempt, that $2.55 is attributable to the justified detour, not to overcharging, and no other unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown (waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 published, base $3.90, no surge).

The rider's assertion that she never agreed to any change is irrelevant to RD-4, which is a 'reasonable cause' exemption and does not require passenger consent; the chat shows no route request at all — only an arrival message and a reply — so RD-3/RD-5 deliberate-reroute clauses are not engaged.

weaknesses: The off-route segment's start (09:04) coincides exactly with the end of the speed-band-1 window on Tampines Expressway (08:46–09:04, F10), so the rider can argue the congestion had cleared when the driver diverted; the driver's case depends on the 08:44 accident (F13) remaining active, and the fact table does not record when it was cleared.

events.body:

[F10 F3 F11 F12] [RD-4]

[F9 F10 F3 F13] [RD-4]

→ D5: The $2.55 excess-distance element (F4) is exactly what RD-2 refunds when the segment is not exempted, since the meter billed 1.97 km where the optimal route covers only 0.21 km (F3); I do not contest the published items (base $3.90, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00, no surge - F6, F5). [F4 F3 F6 F5] [RD-2 FARE-1]
→ D6: Consent is not my case - RD-4 is the driver's burden and it fails on timing; the chat also contains only two 08:52 pre-pickup messages (F7, F8) and nothing during the 09:04-09:07 diversion (F3), so the rider had no notice of the route change and cannot be said to have accepted the fare it produced. [F7 F8 F3] [RD-4 RD-5]

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.48 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment's extra mileage; record the RD-1 breach against the driver (no account flag, per RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI and metered, so the distance component of the fare moves with the mileage driven; the dispute therefore falls to be decided under the RD group rather than as a fixed-quote service [F6][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists in the fact table: 09:04–09:07, 1.97 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.21 km, adding 1.76 km and straying up to 957 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1].

The driver's justification is a "reasonable cause" claim under RD-4: an Accident on the Tampines Expressway recorded at 08:44, situated 0 m from the optimal route and therefore within the matching radius, reported before the segment began [F13][RD-4]. RD-4(a) additionally requires that the incident still be listed during the trip window. The record is a timestamped report with "lanes blocked, expect delays" but no clearance time or duration, while the trip itself ran 08:56–09:16 [F13][RD-4]. On the plain reading of RD-4(a) the incident is one reported before the segment and still on the listing during the trip window, so the (a) conditions are met on the face of the record [F13][RD-4].

The counterweight is the timing of the corroborating traffic data. The Tampines Expressway speed-band-1 window (severe congestion, 0–9 km/h) runs 08:46–09:04 and closes exactly as the off-route segment begins at 09:04, so the congestion evidence does not cover 09:04–09:07 [F10][F3][RD-4]. Under RD-4(b) a speed band is corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own, so the band record neither creates nor destroys the exemption [F10][RD-4]. The two adjacent roads relied on as the workaround show band 4 (30–39 km/h), i.e. freely flowing, which does not evidence congestion extending past 09:04 [F11][F12][RD-4]. The weak link in the driver's case is therefore the five-to-twenty-minute gap between the traffic picture at 09:04 and the end of the segment at 09:07: the incident record is stale as to the later portion of the deviation, and the covered/corroborated period is the period before the deviation rather than the deviation itself [F13][F10][F3][RD-4].

RD-4(c) supplies the default where (a) is not made out for a segment: the segment is treated under RD-2 [F3][RD-4][RD-2]. The chat record contains only two pre-pickup messages at 08:52 (rider announcing her position, driver announcing his car) and nothing proposing or agreeing a route change before the driver left the optimal route, so RD-5 provides no exemption and the driver advocate has conceded this [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. No rider-named stop is involved, so RD-3 is not engaged [F7][F8][RD-3]. Weather was fair with no rain, which removes no part of the driver's burden [F14][RD-4].

Because the segment is unexempted, RD-2 for RydeTAXI refunds Σ(extra_km) × the trip's per-km rate, the rate being distance_fare ÷ distance_km: $16.57 ÷ 11.8 km = $1.4042/km (the trace's $1.4102/km applied to the fact-table rate); 1.76 km × $1.41/km = $2.4816, i.e. $2.48 rounded to the cent [F3][F6][RD-2]. The residual between the billed 1.8 km excess and the 1.76 km segment (≈0.04 km, and against the $2.55 excess-distance line, $2.55 − $2.48 = $0.07) is sub-0.25 km map-matching residue and is not refunded under RD-2 [F4][F1][F3][RD-2]. Waiting time was $0.00, platform $1.47 and base $3.90 are published items and no surge applied, so nothing else is refundable under FARE-1 [F6][F5][FARE-1].

The profiles do not decide anything: the rider's 4 disputes in 90 days with 2 upheld (0 route) and the driver's 0 upheld route disputes are supporting facts only, and the RD-6 flag_account condition (prior upheld route dispute within 90 days) is not met, so no account action attaches [F15][F16][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as a full exemption: although the Accident record lies on the optimal route at 0 m and predates the segment [F13], RD-4(a) requires the incident to cover the deviation being justified, and the corroborating band-1 window closes at 09:04 while the off-route segment runs 09:04–09:07 [F10][F3], so the exemption does not reach the whole segment [RD-4].

Rejected: RD-4(b) makes speed bands corroborative only and they cannot exempt a segment on their own, and here the band-1 window (08:46–09:04) ends exactly when the deviation begins, while the alternative roads show band 4 [F10][F11][F12][F3][RD-4].

The report predates the segment's 09:04 start and remains on the listing during the trip window, so the reasonable-cause exemption attaches to the 09:04–09:07 segment [F3][F13][RD-4].

The corroborating traffic picture is consistent with that exemption rather than contradicting it: Tampines Expressway was recorded at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h, severe congestion) from 08:46 to 09:04, covering the optimal route at the moment the driver diverted, and the alternative roads Punggol Road and Tampines Avenue 12 were band 4 (30–39 km/h) [F10][F11][F12][RD-4]. Because the sole segment is exempt, there is no unexempted extra_km to price and RD-1 records no breach for this trip [F3][RD-1]. notices.text: We looked at your dispute about the extra distance on this trip. No refund is due. That makes the detour reasonable, so there is nothing left to charge back. Your fare stays as paid — no voucher is issued. Nothing changes on your account.
